subject: MAP: acceptance criteria, exit gates, and test owners (Bedrock Health pilot)
messages:
From: Alex Thompson <alex@bedrockhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bedrockhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & acceptance criteria for pilot

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo today — team loved the latency profile and the artifact caching notes. We agreed internally to run a 6-week pilot focused on:
- Retrieval-augmented responses for clinician notes (throughput target ~120 reqs/min)
- Embedding similarity search for matched clinical guidelines

Procurement asked that we share a clear MAP and explicit acceptance criteria so they can sign off and start the trial procurement flow. Specifically we need:
1) Concrete success metrics and pass/fail thresholds (latency, token cost, recall for retrieval)
2) Clear exit gates if performance regresses or security items remain open
3) Owners for each acceptance test (so our SRE and procurement teams can validate)

I attached the pilot SOW and a short list of must-have checks from our security team. Can you send a MAP draft and an acceptance test roster by Thursday?

Alex
Bedrock Health

Attachments: Bedrock_SOW_v1.pdf (stub), BH-security-checklist.xlsx (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex@bedrockhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@bedrockhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & acceptance criteria for pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Draft MAP attached (MAP-Bedrock-v1.xlsx) and I included a companion markdown that lists acceptance tests and suggested owners (bedrock-acceptance-tests.md). High-level outline below so Procurement has the bullets in-line.

Summary (pilot scope):
- Duration: 6 weeks (production-similar traffic during week 3–5)
- Models: rwd-llm-13b (quantized) for generation; rwd-embed-2 for embeddings
- Environment: Dedicated dev cluster (US-east) with telemetry streaming to Bedrock sandbox

Success criteria (pass = all must-haves met):
1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 420ms for <512 tokens under sustained load (120 reqs/min).
2) Throughput: system sustains 120 reqs/min for 30 continuous minutes with <1% error rate.
3) Retrieval recall: top-3 recall >= 78% on the provided clinical query set (see acceptance-tests doc).
4) Cost target: per-token cost <= $0.0009 (based on batching and KV cache).
5) Security baseline: SOC2 evidence provided; OIDC + Kerberos SSO validated; encryption-at-rest verified.

Exit gates (auto-fail triggers):
- Any security control marked "open" by Bedrock security after week 2 that is not owner-assigned and scheduled for remediation.
- Sustained 95th pctl latency > 700ms for 3 consecutive measurement windows (30 min each).
- Error rate > 3% for > 10 minutes during a smoke-run.

Acceptance tests (examples):
- Latency smoke: 500 synthetic requests across 5 instance types, measure p50/p95/p99. Owner: Ben Carter.
- Throughput soak: 45-minute soak at 120 rpm; look for queue growth and tail latency. Owner: Priyom Das.
- Retrieval recall: run canonical query suite (30 queries) and compare against labeled ground truth. Owner: Bedrock data team (point person: Alex Thompson).
- Security evidence: provide SOC2 report excerpt + KMS access logs for key rotation. Owner: Marissa Cole / Redwood Security.

Attachments referenced: MAP-Bedrock-v1.xlsx (MAP with timeline, milestones, and signoff matrix), bedrock-acceptance-tests.md (test cases and owners).

Next steps: Ben and Priyom — quick review of owners and suggested test scripts? Alex — if this aligns I can put the MAP into a versioned DocuSign/Procurement folder so your procurement team can start paperwork.

—Marissa
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-Bedrock-v1.xlsx (stub), bedrock-acceptance-tests.md (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Thompson <alex@bedrockhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@bedrockhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Apr 2025 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & acceptance criteria for pilot

Marissa — quick notes from my end after skimming the MAP and the test list:

Inline comments:
- Latency smoke: add a warm-up phase to prime KV cache and measure cold vs warm. Suggest p95 warm <= 420ms; cold can be relaxed to p95 <= 900ms.
- Throughput soak: define fail/succeed multiple times (3 out of 4 windows) to avoid flaking on spiky infra events.
- Error classification: separate client-errors (4xx) from server-errors (5xx) and only count 5xx towards the error-rate exit gate.

Suggested test fixtures (I can take these):
1) smoke-latency.yml — small harness that runs across sequence lengths [64, 256, 512] with deterministic prompts. (Owner: Ben)
2) soak-120rpm.yml — scaled harness hitting the dedicated pool with a synthetic mix (70% gen, 30% embed). (Owner: Priyom)
3) retrieval-eval.ipynb — notebook that computes recall@k and NDCG; will publish metrics to the shared Drive for Bedrock review. (Owner: Ben + Alex)

One business ask: for the cost target we should include an escape clause if real user traffic shape produces significantly higher token counts — propose a tolerance band of +18% on token cost for the pilot with a renegotiation checkpoint at week 4.

If folks agree I'll add the fixtures into the Map workbook and push updated attachments.

Ben
Head of Technical Ops — Redwood Inference

Alex / Procurement —

Thanks Ben and Priyom for the quick turn. Attached is MAP-Bedrock-v1.xlsx (updated) and bedrock-acceptance-tests.md (includes test fixtures and owners). Key updates since the draft:
- Warm/cold latency separation added to smoke tests (Ben).
- Soak window failure tolerance and repeat-window rule added (Priyom).
- Cost tolerance clause: +18% tolerance with week-4 renegotiation checkpoint (business-agreed).

Procurement checklist for Bedrock to begin purchase order:
1) Confirm PO amount reflects committed Dedicated dev cluster + 6-week pilot duration (line items in MAP workbook).
2) Sign the MAP acknowledgement sheet in the workbook (sheet: signoff).
3) Provide point of contact for Bedrock security validation; Bedrock should grant temporary KMS access to the Redwood audit account for verification traces.

If Procurement confirms today we can start the contract workflow and schedule the pilot kickoff for Monday 2025-04-21.

Next steps we will take on our side:
- Ben will publish smoke-latency.yml and retrieval-eval.ipynb to the shared Drive by Friday.
- Priyom will provision the soak harness and validate autoscaling guardrails.
- I will open a DocuSign envelope with the MAP acknowledgement and attach the updated acceptance-tests doc.

Alex — please confirm the Bedrock point person for security validation and confirm you are OK with the week-4 cost checkpoint.

Best,
Marissa
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference
